title: Evals change observability: root-cause linking, priority routing, and webhook payload spec
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Surface evals-based regressions that are attributable to model/config changes in the Console, and route high-confidence regressions to the correct channel (Slack/PagerDuty) with durable dedupe and rich root-cause context. This ticket covers UI surface design (timeline, commit/change grouping), backend event modeling (change_id, snapshot diff, eval run id), alert dedupe/suppression rules, and the webhook payload contract for downstream integrations (Slack blocks, PagerDuty event fields).
acceptance_criteria: Console timeline shows eval runs grouped by change_id and links back to commit/PR when provided
Alerts for model/config regressions are routed to Slack channels and PagerDuty services according to routing policy rules
Alert dedupe prevents noisy repeats for the same change across a configurable suppression window (default 2 hours)
Webhook payload contains standardized fields: change_id, change_summary, eval_suite_id, metric_deltas, confidence_score, example_fails, link_to_console
Backend exposes a stable events API for 'eval_regression_detected' with documented idempotency keys
E2E smoke test demonstrates a simulated config change producing a single routed alert (Slack + PD) and a suppressed duplicate within window
non_goals: Automatic remediation or rollback of model/config changes
Replacing full incident management — we only send routed signals to PD/Slack, not handle escalations beyond PD integration
Full auto-triage of false positives — initial phase relies on configurable thresholds and manual tuning
tradeoffs: Tighter dedupe windows reduce noise but increase the chance of masking distinct regressions from rapid sequential changes
Embedding rich example context in webhook payloads increases webhook size and latency — we'll limit examples to top 3 failing cases
High-confidence routing requires more conservative thresholds which can delay noisy alerts landing in PD; we will make thresholds configurable per project
